proposal:
Step 42 composed enqueue ownership repair proposal — STATIC, UNAPPLIED, UNEXECUTED
Composition: lead/verify-step42-composed-4e0bfc0e, accepted-main parent 4e0bfc0e
Status: proposal only. No production source is changed by this artifact.

CONTRACT

Sim.enqueue is a success-only ownership transfer.

- Before the call, the caller exclusively owns retained.
- On any error, the caller still owns retained. No mailbox entry, trace entry, or newly published runnable bit/wake retains or exposes it. next_seq is unchanged.
- On success, exactly one mailbox entry owns retained. The caller must not free it.
- Sequence assignment, FIFO order, sender/to values, seeded trace order, scheduler selection, and wake behavior remain unchanged on success.
- Every allocation and other fallible preparation happens before runnable publication. Setting the runnable bit and stirring/waking its scheduler are the final, infallible publication step.
- This is not a consumes-on-error interface.

SOURCE WITNESSES

1. toolchain/src/sim.zig:1023-1029
   Current enqueue increments next_seq, appends the mailbox entry, then can fail in Turns.markRunnable or trace.append. A caller errdefer can therefore free a parcel already reachable from the mailbox.
2. toolchain/src/turns.zig:1023-1029
   markRunnable can fail only while resizing the runnable bitset, before set/stir. Split preparation from publication.
3. All enqueue calls, from the whole toolchain/src reference search:
   - sim.zig:718 — Sim.send, fresh ParcelValue.
   - sim.zig:817 — dueLater, ParcelValue popped from the timer heap.
   - sim.zig:849 — askInline, fresh ParcelValue.
   - sim.zig:1180 — deliver commit, one value in a batch-held outbox.
   - turns.zig:1242 — Turns.ask, fresh ParcelValue.
   - sources.zig:252 — runtime source delivery, fresh ParcelValue; includes every Step44 Chunk/Closed/Idle delivery.
   - surface.zig:386 — Runtime.send, fresh ParcelValue.
4. toolchain/src/sim.zig:1187-1194 and turns.zig:1350-1362
   Pending answers have the same prefix-retirement problem. A routed prefix remains in p.answers if a later route fails. Turns.answer removes awaiting before answers.put can fail and currently frees reply on error.
5. toolchain/src/sim.zig:1075-1097,1251-1258
   A mailbox entry is removed before logMessage can fail. This is another success-only transfer seam: on log insertion failure the entry is no longer mailbox-owned and must remain locally owned or be freed.
6. toolchain/src/sim.zig:1183-1184
   A failed events append leaves p.emits owning the retained values, but deliver currently has no commit-error cleanup for them.

SMALLEST PRODUCTION CHANGE

Exact proposed production paths:
- toolchain/src/sim.zig
- toolchain/src/turns.zig
- toolchain/src/sources.zig
- toolchain/src/surface.zig

No runtime/mo_rt.c change: native enqueue and allocation are not recoverable error-returning paths. No generic owner/guard type, queue wrapper, or consumes-on-error convention is proposed.

A. Make enqueue preflight every fallible operation.

Pseudocode in sim.zig:

    pub fn enqueue(sim, from, to, retained) Error!u64 {
        const target = &sim.procs.items[to];

        try target.mailbox.ensureUnusedCapacity(sim.gpa, 1);
        if (sim.schedule != null)
            try sim.trace.ensureUnusedCapacity(sim.gpa, 1);
        if (sim.turns) |t|
            try t.prepareRunnable(to);

        const seq = sim.next_seq;
        sim.next_seq += 1;
        target.mailbox.appendAssumeCapacity(.{ .retained = retained, .seq = seq });
        if (sim.schedule != null)
            sim.trace.appendAssumeCapacity(.{ .from = from, .to = to,
                .message = retained.value, .took = false });
        if (sim.turns) |t|
            t.markRunnable(to);
        return seq;
    }

The implementation must use the Zig 0.16 capacity/assume-capacity APIs available to ArrayList and AutoHashMap; names above are pseudocode until implementation. next_seq moves only in the non-fallible commit section.

B. Split scheduler preparation from publication in turns.zig.

    pub fn prepareRunnable(t, id) Error!void {
        const s = t.scheds[t.homeOf(id)];
        if (id >= s.runnable.bit_length)
            try s.runnable.resize(t.gpa,
                @max(2 * s.runnable.bit_length, id + 64), false);
    }

    pub fn markRunnable(t, id) void {
        const s = t.scheds[t.homeOf(id)];
        assert(id < s.runnable.bit_length);
        s.runnable.set(id);
        t.stir(s);
    }

surface.hold's resume path becomes an infallible markRunnable call. A queued process is representable because the successful enqueue that created its queue entry already completed prepareRunnable.

C. Scope fresh-value cleanup only across enqueue.

Sim.send already has a local retained plus errdefer. It becomes correct once enqueue is success-only; no new ownership mechanism is needed.

askInline, Turns.ask, sources.send, and surface.send must use a lexical block so the cleanup scope ends immediately after successful enqueue:

    const seq = blk: {
        const retained = try sim.parcelValue(message);
        errdefer retained.free();
        break :blk try sim.enqueue(from, to, retained);
    };

A function-wide errdefer is prohibited: later ask/delivery work is fallible after the mailbox has taken ownership.

Turns.ask must reserve one awaiting-map entry before enqueue, then use an assume-capacity insertion after enqueue. The runtime lock prevents a woken target from running before awaiting and deadline are installed. This avoids publishing an ask whose awaiting insertion then fails.

surface.send should prepare its fallible return value and copied event text before enqueue, then use the scoped transfer, non-fallible record, and prebuilt return. This preserves the row's all-preparation-before-publication error behavior; it is not needed to free a mailbox-owned parcel after success.

D. A popped due timer owns its parcel until enqueue succeeds.

In each dueLater iteration, install an error cleanup immediately after popLater. Down/full paths continue to free explicitly. On enqueue error the iteration-scoped cleanup frees the popped parcel. On enqueue success the lexical scope exits normally and the mailbox owns it. A cleanup from a completed earlier iteration must not remain armed when a later iteration fails.

E. Retire a committed outbox prefix without allocation or shifting.

Remove the up-front `sim.held -= p.outbox.items.len`. Iterate by pointer. After each down/drop, successful pushLater, or successful enqueue:

- overwrite only that slot's retained field with the empty ParcelValue sentinel (`value=.none`, `parcel=null`);
- decrement sim.held by one.

Install one commit-error cleanup that frees only the still-owned suffix/nonempty slots, decrements held for those slots, and clears the outbox. On the normal path, clear the array once after all entries transfer. This adds no per-send allocation and no orderedRemove/memmove; normal work remains one linear pass. A later failure cannot leave a successfully transferred prefix double-owned.

`pushLater` remains a success-only transfer for allocation errors: failed heap append leaves the caller owner; success either stores the value or, when exiting, drops/frees it. Retire the outbox slot only after pushLater returns success.

SCHEDULER SYNCHRONIZATION

- With multiple schedulers, turns.zig's runtime mutex covers mailbox, trace, runnable bitsets, awaiting/answers maps, source pumping, delivery commit, and runtime rows. VM send/ask opcodes enter through Vm.lockRuntime. Scheduler loops and main hold the same lock while manipulating runtime tables.
- enqueue performs capacity preparation and its non-fallible commit while that lock is held. markRunnable may wake another scheduler, but that scheduler cannot inspect the mailbox until the current holder releases the runtime lock.
- The mailbox and seeded send trace are committed before runnable publication. Therefore a recipient cannot take a message before its trace entry exists.
- With one scheduler, markRunnable is same-thread publication. Without Turns, Mo.Sim is single-threaded. The same order preserves deterministic FIFO and seeded trace behavior.
- stir/rouse remains the existing non-fallible notification path; wake write errors remain intentionally ignored as before.

ADJACENT REQUIRED OWNERSHIP SCOPE

These are called out explicitly rather than hidden inside the enqueue change.

1. Pending-answer routing (required in the same repair).
   - Make Turns.answer success-only: if no waiter exists, freeing the reply is successful consumption. Otherwise reserve answers-map capacity before removing awaiting; then fetchRemove, assume-capacity insert, and wake without fallible work. On reserve error, awaiting remains and the caller still owns reply. Remove its consumes-on-error errdefer.
   - In no-turns routePacked, reserve answered-map capacity before insertion. On reserve error the PendingAnswer remains caller-owned.
   - routeAnswer creates a fresh parcel and therefore needs cleanup scoped only across the success-only route call.
   - Iterate p.answers by pointer. After each successful route, retire that slot's ParcelValue and only then remove its kept sequence. On a later failure, free/clear only the remaining owned answers. No routed prefix remains double-owned.

2. Committed emits (required commit-error cleanup in sim.zig).
   If events.appendSlice fails, free and clear p.emits because the update commit is aborting and events never took ownership. If append succeeds, clear p.emits immediately; sim.events then owns the values. This is a direct scoped cleanup, not a generic abstraction.

3. Mailbox-to-log transfer (additional required scope in sim.zig).
   Preflight log capacity before advancing/removing the mailbox entry, accounting for the log_kept eviction slot. Then remove the mailbox entry, evict/free the old log item if required, and appendAssumeCapacity. This keeps entry ownership in the mailbox on preparation failure and avoids leaking a removed entry. It is adjacent to enqueue but not an enqueue caller change.

The proposal does not expand into every fatal-OOM state transition (for example downKept's sequence-list semantics). Those have no newly duplicated Parcel owner in the reviewed path and require a separate transaction/error-semantics decision.

SUCCESS/ERROR OWNERSHIP SUMMARY BY ENQUEUE CALLER

- Sim.send: fresh; existing errdefer owns until enqueue success.
- dueLater: popped timer; iteration cleanup owns until enqueue success.
- askInline: fresh; block-scoped cleanup owns until enqueue success; later ask errors do not touch mailbox ownership.
- deliver outbox: batch-held; retire each successful slot and clean only the remaining suffix on error.
- Turns.ask: fresh; preflight awaiting, block-scoped cleanup across enqueue, assume-capacity awaiting insertion while lock remains held.
- sources.send: fresh; block-scoped cleanup across enqueue, then return.
- surface.send: fresh; prepare result/event text first, block-scoped cleanup across enqueue, then only non-fallible publication bookkeeping.

NON-GOALS

- No blanket consumes-on-error rule.
- No generic ownership guard or queue abstraction.
- No changes to native C runtime ownership.
- No retries, warning suppression, allocator fallback, or swallowed OutOfMemory.
- No pointer-identity or empty-container-only reclamation claim.
- No runtime, build, formatter, benchmark, commit, final report, or AFTER freeze from this proposal.

STATIC TEST/PROBE DRAFT — DO NOT APPLY OR EXECUTE

Dependencies when Parcel destruction must be observed:
- composed copy of test-only-parcel-audit.patch
- std.testing.FailingAllocator
- Vm.parcel_audit and Vm.parcel_allocator from that private patch
No non-test runtime instrumentation is proposed.

Common observable payload

Use a dynamic Chunk-style payload rather than an atom or pointer check:

    Payload(parts: [0, 65, 0xE2, 0x82, 0xAC, 0xF0, 0x28, 0x8C, 0x28, 66],
            label: "enqueue-owned")

Every successful-owner assertion reads the complete list and label. Reclamation assertions print raw allocator and ParcelAudit counts before asserting:

    case=<name> allocator_attempts=N induced_failure=true
    case=<name> allocated=N destroyed=N live=N

A green cleanup case requires allocated > 0, destroyed == allocated, live == 0. A live owner at an intentionally interrupted commit is counted explicitly, then ordinary cleanup must bring live to zero. Pointer identity, a null parcel field, or an empty list alone is not reclamation proof.

AUTOMATIC CONTROL A — enqueue trace-reserve failure is atomic
Location if accepted: sim.zig test. Does not require ParcelAudit for the state contract; add the private audit form below for destruction proof.

Arrange:
1. Seeded Sim so enqueue must append a send trace.
2. Start a target process.
3. Reserve exactly one mailbox slot in advance; leave trace with no spare slot.
4. Record before_seq, mailbox length, trace length.
5. Give sim.gpa a FailingAllocator armed so trace.ensureUnusedCapacity is the failing preflight.
6. Call enqueue with a caller-owned raw ParcelValue.

Assert after OutOfMemory:
- next_seq == before_seq.
- target mailbox length is unchanged (zero in the isolated case).
- trace length is unchanged.
- no runnable state exists in this no-Turns case.
- caller's retained value remains readable and is still caller-owned.

This fails on the current implementation because mailbox append and next_seq mutation happen before trace.append fails.

AUTOMATIC CONTROL B — runnable resize failure is atomic
Location if accepted: turns.zig or sim.zig focused test.

Arrange:
1. Minimal one-scheduler Turns attached to Sim.
2. Target mailbox already has spare capacity; seeded trace is disabled.
3. Target id is beyond scheduler.runnable.bit_length.
4. Turns.gpa is a FailingAllocator armed at runnable.resize.
5. Record before_seq, mailbox length, runnable bit length/state and wake state.
6. Call enqueue with caller-owned retained.

Assert after OutOfMemory:
- next_seq unchanged.
- mailbox unchanged.
- target runnable bit remains unset.
- scheduler was not stirred/roused and wake state did not publish work.
- caller still owns retained.

After the repair, this fails in prepareRunnable before commit. It directly guards the lock/publication ordering rather than only checking a freed parcel.

PRIVATE AUDIT CONTROL C — Sim.send frees a fresh parcel when post-mailbox preparation fails
Private smoke unless the builtin.is_test ParcelAudit hook is accepted as permanent test support.

Arrange as control A or B, but set sim.packs=true and call Sim.send with the dynamic Payload. Vm.parcel_allocator remains healthy and audited; only sim.gpa or Turns.gpa fails.

Assert raw observations before any balance assertion:
- OutOfMemory.
- mailbox, trace, runnable and next_seq unchanged.
- ParcelAudit allocated=1 destroyed=1 live=0.
- FailingAllocator reports the intended failed reserve.

Pre-repair discriminator: mailbox length becomes one while Sim.send's current errdefer destroys the parcel, creating a published dangling value.

PRIVATE AUDIT CONTROL D — Step44 source_send packing/queue failure
Location in a private sources.zig test patch so private `send` is exercised directly.

Arrange:
1. Construct a target process and Sim with packs=true.
2. Keep Vm.gpa/heap and Vm.parcel_allocator healthy; attach ParcelAudit.
3. After setup, replace only sim.gpa with a FailingAllocator that fails mailbox capacity preparation.
4. Use sources.send(target, "Chunk", fields=[complete dynamic byte list]).
5. Keep mailbox, trace and runnable initially empty; record next_seq.

Assert:
- sources.send returns OutOfMemory.
- no mailbox or trace entry, no runnable publication, next_seq unchanged.
- the attempted message is reported by setup diagnostics as Chunk with the complete byte-list payload.
- raw ParcelAudit allocated=1 destroyed=1 live=0.
- raw failing allocator counters identify the queue-capacity failure.

This is the original source-send pack-then-queue ownership hole. It must not be reduced to `mailbox.len == 0` or `parcel == null`.

PRIVATE AUDIT CONTROL E — popped due timer owns until enqueue success
Arrange:
1. Create one audited packed delayed message carrying the dynamic Payload.
2. Advance time so dueLater pops it.
3. Arm failure in enqueue preflight.

Assert after OutOfMemory:
- later heap is empty because this fatal attempt popped the timer.
- target mailbox/trace/runnable and next_seq are unchanged.
- allocated=1 destroyed=1 live=0: the iteration-scoped owner cleaned the popped parcel.

Then run a green twin without failure:
- dueLater returns true.
- target mailbox contains exactly one message with the complete payload.
- after delivery/log cleanup, audit returns live=0.

PRIVATE AUDIT CONTROL F — fresh ask cleanup scopes end at successful transfer
Two subcases.

F1 askInline enqueue failure:
- packs=true, dynamic ask message, enqueue preflight fails.
- mailbox, waiting, answered and next_seq unchanged.
- allocated=1 destroyed=1 live=0.

F2 Turns.ask enqueue failure:
- reserve/prepare awaiting capacity as production will.
- fail enqueue preparation.
- awaiting and answers maps unchanged; mailbox/runnable unchanged.
- allocated=1 destroyed=1 live=0.

Green twin:
- enqueue succeeds, awaiting contains seq before the runtime lock is released.
- a complete dynamic reply is returned.
- no caller cleanup fires after successful transfer; final teardown returns live=0.

PRIVATE AUDIT CONTROL G — outbox prefix retirement on later failure
Use a minimal compiled update that sends two distinct dynamic payloads, First and Second.

Arrange without per-send failure instrumentation:
1. Pre-reserve sender outbox capacity for both sends before the update.
2. Pre-reserve First target's mailbox/trace/runnable needs so its commit transfer allocates nothing.
3. Leave Second target's mailbox without spare capacity.
4. Arm sim.gpa failure before delivery; parcel allocation uses the separate healthy audited parcel allocator.
5. Deliver the sender update. The first transfer succeeds; the second enqueue preparation fails.

Assert immediately after error:
- First target mailbox has exactly one message whose complete payload is First.
- Second target mailbox is empty.
- sender outbox's First slot is retired and is not treated as an owner.
- sender outbox still owns Second until commit-error cleanup; after that cleanup the outbox is empty.
- sim.held moves from 2 to 1 after First transfer, then to 0 when the failing suffix is cleaned.
- raw audit at the ownership checkpoint distinguishes one mailbox owner and one outbox owner; final cleanup prints allocated=2 destroyed=2 live=0.
- no double free under the private audit allocator.

The control must not assert only outbox length or sentinel fields; it must read First from its mailbox and prove both parcel destructions in final counts.

PRIVATE AUDIT CONTROL H — pending-answer prefix retirement
Use an update that holds two replies and answers both with distinct dynamic strings.

Arrange:
1. First seq has no waiter, so routePacked successfully drops/frees First without map allocation.
2. Second seq still waits; arm answered-map or Turns.answers capacity failure for its route.
3. Commit the update.

Assert after error:
- First is no longer in kept and its answer slot is retired; its parcel destruction is counted once.
- Second remains in kept and owned by the still-unrouted answer until commit-error cleanup.
- awaiting is unchanged for Second if threaded Turns.answer preparation failed.
- answered/answers has no partial Second entry.
- final cleanup produces allocated=2 destroyed=2 live=0, with no double free.

Green twin:
- both answers route according to their waiter state.
- the waiting reply's complete dynamic string is observed.
- pending answers and kept state are empty as expected.
- final live=0.

PRIVATE/AUTOMATIC CONTROL I — mailbox-to-log preparation failure
State assertions can remain automatic; Parcel counts use the private audit hook.

Arrange:
1. Mailbox contains one audited dynamic message.
2. Log has no spare capacity and no eviction slot is available for this mode.
3. Arm failure in log capacity preparation before deliver removes the mailbox entry.

Assert:
- deliver returns OutOfMemory.
- mailbox head/length and complete message payload are unchanged.
- log is unchanged.
- next delivery can take the same FIFO message after the allocator is restored.
- after delivery and teardown, allocated=1 destroyed=1 live=0.

CLASSIFICATION

Keep as automatic behavior tests after implementation:
- A: enqueue trace preparation is atomic.
- B: runnable preparation failure publishes nothing.
- I state/FIFO portion: mailbox-to-log preparation leaves the message queued.
These guard observable success-only transfer, sequence, FIFO and scheduling state without relying on private production instrumentation.

Keep as private smoke evidence unless the existing builtin.is_test audit hook is accepted:
- C through H and I's raw destruction half.
They need precise Parcel allocation/destruction observations or allocator choreography. The hook compiles to void outside Zig tests; no runtime flag, public row, production counter, or native change is allowed.

For every private failure run, immediately run its green twin and record raw allocator plus allocated/destroyed/live output before assertions. Do not infer reclamation from pointers, list lengths, or successful process exit.

Design decisions/refinements:
1. Enqueue success-only: reserve mailbox and optional trace capacity before any publication. Prefer retaining the existing fallible Turns.markRunnable API: call it after queue/trace reserves, immediately BEFORE an entirely infallible sequence/mailbox/trace commit while holding the existing runtime lock. Its only fallible resize precedes set/stir; a woken scheduler cannot inspect runtime tables until unlock. Lead reviewed vm.lockRuntime321–326 and Turns lock/stir/rouse. This avoids introducing prepare/publish methods or narrowing surface.hold's existing guarantee. Add a concise lock/infallible-tail comment; confirm no caller releases/reenters between marking and commit. If you find a real counterexample, stop that design and report source; do not silently assume it. No fallible operation after marking, no seq/mailbox/trace/runnable mutation on error. Preserve FIFO, sender and successful trace semantics.
2. Fresh/popped parcels: scoped cleanup until transfer, never beyond later fallible ask work. Function scope is fine only when no fallible work follows enqueue, as in existing Sim.send. Awaiting capacity must be ready before publishing a threaded ask. Surface send prepares its fallible return/event copy first, frees that copied text if publication fails, and retains original successful event behavior.
3. For outbox and pending-answer batches use local committed-prefix cursors plus error-only suffix cleanup, not per-slot empty sentinels. Sentinels add avoidable normal-path stores and conflate a legitimate raw .none reply with retirement. Clear each buffer on complete success, reset its cursor before any later fallible action. Preserve held accounting and remove kept sequences only after successful answer routing. On error free only still-owned suffixes, never the transferred prefix. No per-message allocation, normal-path shifting or new queue abstraction.
4. Put owned-buffer error cleanup early enough to cover errors before later commit phases too: if an outbox transfer fails, p.emits and p.answers already contain owned parcels; their cleanup cannot be installed only after the outbox loop. Likewise review non-Crash update errors before commit. Reacquire Proc by id in cleanup where update/other work can grow procs; do not capture a stale element pointer. Keep existing Crash behavior, do not double-clean it, and do not claim transaction rollback/retry semantics for fatal OOM.
5. Adjacent scope approved: success-only Turns.answer/routePacked with map capacity before awaiting removal; fresh routeAnswer cleanup; retained emits cleanup; mailbox-to-log capacity preflight before mailbox head/removal, preserving exact packed eviction and raw no-packs behavior. Controls: A trace-reserve failure and B runnable-resize failure must discriminate current partial publication and preserve caller payload/state. I must leave the exact FIFO head deliverable after log-preflight failure.
